sources.entry: OpenSpatial - Open-source spatial audio for any headphones, playing every app as 7.1 surround with head tracking. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/dortanes/openspatial) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: OpenSpatial is a macOS app that turns any wired or wireless headphones into 7.1 surround sound with optional camera-based head tracking, applied to every app on the Mac.
summary.what_it_does: It routes system audio through its own Core Audio driver (based on BlackHole) and renders it as spatial 7.1 surround over headphones, for browsers, players, games and music apps. Head tracking uses the Mac's camera so the front stays fixed in place as the listener moves. Stereo can be spread to virtual speakers, and an AI surround mode (HT-Demucs, run through Core ML on the Neural Engine) pulls the voice out of stereo and places it in front. Users can choose virtual room presets (two studio control rooms, a small and large concert hall, or no room), boost quiet apps, and view a live 3D map of the sound. A Safari extension requests the 5.1 Netflix track on netflix.com, and the README says Windows games can play in 7.1 through Wine.
use_cases: watch movies in 5.1 on Netflix in Safari
spatial audio for games on Mac
play Windows games in 7.1 through Wine
boost quiet apps and even out volume
how_to_run: Download the latest version from Releases (needs Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later).
Move OpenSpatial to Applications and open it; allow the audio driver install and microphone access.
Open Settings and select your headphones under Sound → Output device.
Build from source: git clone the repo, cd openspatial, then run app/build.sh (requires Xcode 26 or later and uv).
notable: Netflix 5.1 via a Safari extension that only runs on netflix.com
Head tracking using the Mac camera, with frames never stored
AI voice extraction that places dialogue in front, like a cinema center speaker
Room presets built from WDR and TH Köln impulse-response data
Works with Wine so Windows games can play in 7.1
caveats: Requires Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later.
AI surround adds about 2 seconds of latency to stereo playback, so it is best for music rather than videos or games.
Windows game support needs Wine 11.7 or later and was tested only with CrossOver Preview.
